scope: Additional selected people across the Hebrew Bible and New Testament. This is a cited reading index, not a complete prosopography or independent historical verification.
sourcePolicy: The provided passage citations support the naming and descriptions used for the indexed narrative figures. Homonyms and uncertain traditional identifications are distinguished. No external archaeological or literary source should be taken as proving a whole narrative.

people.name: Adam
people.disambiguation: The Adam of the Genesis creation account, not a later namesake.
people.summary: Genesis describes Adam as the first man in the garden narrative.

people.name: Eve
people.disambiguation: The first woman of the Genesis narrative.
people.summary: Genesis depicts Eve in the garden narrative and as mother of Cain and Abel.

people.name: Cain
people.disambiguation: Adam and Eve's son in Genesis, not another similarly named figure.
people.summary: Cain is identified as Abel's brother in the account of the first murder.

people.name: Abel
people.disambiguation: The Abel of Genesis 4, later recalled in Hebrews.
people.summary: Abel is Cain's brother whose offering and death are recorded in Genesis.

people.name: Seth
people.disambiguation: Seth son of Adam, not other people of similar names.
people.summary: Genesis identifies Seth as a son of Adam and Eve and traces his descendants.

people.name: Enoch son of Jared
people.disambiguation: The Enoch in Genesis 5, distinct from Cain's son in Genesis 4.
people.summary: Genesis describes Enoch as one who walked with God.

people.name: Noah
people.disambiguation: Noah of the flood narrative, not other people called Noah.
people.summary: Genesis tells the story of Noah, the ark, the flood and the post-flood covenant.

people.name: Shem
people.disambiguation: Shem son of Noah, not an entire later ethnic or linguistic group.
people.summary: Genesis names Shem among Noah's sons and traces his descendants.

people.name: Ham son of Noah
people.disambiguation: Ham son of Noah, not an ancient state or modern racial grouping.
people.summary: Genesis identifies Ham as one of Noah's sons.

people.name: Japheth
people.disambiguation: The Japheth in the Table of Nations, not a modern nation.
people.summary: Japheth is one of Noah's sons in Genesis.

people.name: Lot
people.disambiguation: Lot the nephew of Abram, not the English word lot.
people.summary: Genesis depicts Lot as Abram's relative who settles near Sodom and survives the city's destruction.

people.name: Hagar
people.disambiguation: Hagar in the Abraham and Sarah household.
people.summary: Genesis narrates the experiences of Hagar, an Egyptian servant, and her son Ishmael.

people.name: Ishmael son of Abraham
people.disambiguation: Ishmael in the ancestral narrative, not a collective label for later peoples.
people.summary: Genesis identifies Ishmael as the son of Abraham and Hagar.

people.name: Rebekah
people.disambiguation: Wife of Isaac and mother of twins Esau and Jacob.
people.summary: Genesis describes Rebekah's marriage to Isaac and the birth of Esau and Jacob.

people.name: Esau
people.disambiguation: Esau son of Isaac, not identical to every later reference to Edom.
people.summary: Genesis identifies Esau as Jacob's twin and narrates their later reconciliation.

people.name: Leah
people.disambiguation: Leah, daughter of Laban, distinct from Rachel.
people.summary: Genesis names Leah as Jacob's wife and the mother of several of his sons.

people.name: Rachel
people.disambiguation: Rachel wife of Jacob, distinct from Leah.
people.summary: Genesis recounts Rachel's marriage to Jacob and the birth of Benjamin.

people.name: Judah son of Jacob
people.disambiguation: The patriarch Judah, not the later kingdom of Judah or Judas Iscariot.
people.summary: Genesis identifies Judah as one of Jacob's sons.

people.name: Benjamin son of Jacob
people.disambiguation: Benjamin son of Jacob, not the later tribe as a single person.
people.summary: Genesis identifies Benjamin as the younger son of Rachel and Jacob.

people.name: Jethro
people.disambiguation: Jethro the Midianite priest; the naming traditions involving Reuel require care.
people.summary: Exodus identifies Jethro as Moses' father-in-law and a priest of Midian.

people.name: Zipporah
people.disambiguation: Wife of Moses in the Exodus narratives.
people.summary: Exodus identifies Zipporah as Moses' wife.

people.name: Caleb son of Jephunneh
people.disambiguation: The Caleb son of Jephunneh, not a later person with the name.
people.summary: Caleb appears in the wilderness scouting narrative and receives an inheritance in Joshua.

people.name: Rahab of Jericho
people.disambiguation: Rahab in Joshua, not the poetic sea-monster name Rahab in Job or Psalms.
people.summary: Joshua depicts Rahab sheltering Israelite spies and surviving the city's capture.

people.name: Eleazar son of Aaron
people.disambiguation: Aaron's son and successor, not Eleazar named elsewhere.
people.summary: The priest Eleazar succeeded Aaron in the wilderness narratives.

people.name: Phinehas son of Eleazar
people.disambiguation: The son of Eleazar, not another Phinehas such as Eli's son.
people.summary: Phinehas appears in the priestly traditions of Numbers and Joshua.

people.name: Gideon
people.disambiguation: The judge Gideon, also called Jerubbaal.
people.summary: Judges portrays Gideon leading a small force against Midian.

people.name: Jephthah
people.disambiguation: The judge Jephthah, whose vow is narrated in Judges.
people.summary: Judges describes Jephthah, his military leadership and a controversial vow.

people.name: Samson
people.disambiguation: The judge Samson, not a generic name for strong warriors.
people.summary: Judges tells of Samson's strength, conflicts with Philistines and death.

people.name: Delilah
people.disambiguation: Delilah in Judges 16, distinct from Samson's unnamed wife.
people.summary: Judges identifies Delilah as the woman who learns the secret of Samson's strength.

people.name: Naomi
people.disambiguation: Naomi, Ruth's mother-in-law, not Ruth herself.
people.summary: Ruth describes Naomi's return from Moab and her relationship with Ruth.

people.name: Boaz
people.disambiguation: Boaz in Ruth, not the similarly named temple pillar.
people.summary: Boaz is depicted as a kinsman who marries Ruth.

people.name: Eli the priest
people.disambiguation: Eli at Shiloh, not Elijah or Elisha.
people.summary: First Samuel presents Eli as a priest at Shiloh and mentor to the young Samuel.

people.name: Hannah mother of Samuel
people.disambiguation: Samuel's mother Hannah, distinct from the prophetess Anna in Luke.
people.summary: First Samuel narrates Hannah's prayer and the dedication of her son Samuel.

people.name: Jonathan son of Saul
people.disambiguation: Prince Jonathan, not other Jonathans in Scripture.
people.summary: Jonathan is Saul's son and David's friend in First Samuel.

people.name: Michal daughter of Saul
people.disambiguation: Michal daughter of Saul, not David's other wives.
people.summary: First and Second Samuel identify Michal as a daughter of Saul and wife of David.

people.name: Abigail wife of Nabal
people.disambiguation: Abigail of Carmel in 1 Samuel, distinct from David's sister Abigail.
people.summary: Abigail intervenes between David and Nabal and later becomes David's wife.

people.name: Bathsheba
people.disambiguation: Bathsheba, mother of Solomon, distinct from Abigail.
people.summary: Second Samuel and First Kings describe Bathsheba's relationship to David and her role in Solomon's succession.

people.name: Nathan the prophet
people.disambiguation: The prophet Nathan, not Nathan son of David.
people.summary: Nathan appears as a court prophet confronting David in Second Samuel.

people.name: Absalom
people.disambiguation: Absalom son of David.
people.summary: Second Samuel recounts Absalom's rebellion against his father David.

people.name: Adonijah son of David
people.disambiguation: Son of David, distinct from Solomon.
people.summary: First Kings narrates Adonijah's unsuccessful attempt to claim the throne.

people.name: Zadok the priest
people.disambiguation: Priest associated with the early monarchy, not all later priests called Zadok.
people.summary: Zadok appears as a priest during David's reign and at Solomon's anointing.

people.name: Queen of Sheba
people.disambiguation: The ruler is unnamed in the canonical Kings account; later personal names are not established by it.
people.summary: Kings narrates a visiting queen who tests Solomon with difficult questions.

people.name: Hiram king of Tyre
people.disambiguation: Hiram the king of Tyre, not the similarly named craftsman Hiram.
people.summary: Kings depicts Hiram of Tyre as a ruler supplying materials and skilled labour.

people.name: Omri king of Israel
people.disambiguation: Northern Israelite king, father of Ahab; distinct from the Assyrian shorthand 'House of Omri'.
people.summary: First Kings records Omri's rise and purchase of the hill of Samaria.

people.name: Jezebel
people.disambiguation: Queen in the northern monarchy narratives, not the figurative Jezebel in Revelation.
people.summary: First Kings depicts Jezebel, Ahab's wife, in the Carmel-era and Naboth narratives.

people.name: Jehoshaphat king of Judah
people.disambiguation: King of Judah, not Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud.
people.summary: Kings describes Jehoshaphat as king of Judah during the divided monarchy.

people.name: Uzziah king of Judah
people.disambiguation: The king also called Azariah, not the priest Azariah.
people.summary: Kings and Chronicles describe Uzziah's Judahite reign.

people.name: Ahaz king of Judah
people.disambiguation: Ahaz of Judah, not Ahaziah of Israel or Judah.
people.summary: Second Kings and Isaiah place Ahaz among the Judahite monarchs confronted by regional powers.

people.name: Athaliah
people.disambiguation: Royal woman in Judah, distinct from Jezebel.
people.summary: Second Kings recounts Athaliah's rule and removal from the Judahite throne.

people.name: Naaman the Aramean
people.disambiguation: Naaman in Second Kings, not other people of the same name.
people.summary: Second Kings describes Naaman, an Aramean commander, and his encounter with Elisha.

people.name: Huldah the prophetess
people.disambiguation: Prophetess of Josiah's period, not a priest.
people.summary: Second Kings identifies Huldah as a prophet consulted during Josiah's reign.

people.name: Manasseh king of Judah
people.disambiguation: King of Judah, not Manasseh son of Joseph nor the tribe bearing that name.
people.summary: Second Kings and Chronicles narrate Manasseh's long reign.

people.name: Baruch son of Neriah
people.disambiguation: Baruch associated with Jeremiah, distinct from later figures sharing the name.
people.summary: Jeremiah depicts Baruch as a scribe who records and reads prophetic words.

people.name: Gedaliah son of Ahikam
people.disambiguation: The appointed governor after 586 BCE, not another Gedaliah.
people.summary: Kings and Jeremiah describe Gedaliah's leadership in Judah after Jerusalem's fall.

people.name: Nebuzaradan
people.disambiguation: The imperial officer, distinct from King Nebuchadnezzar.
people.summary: Kings names Nebuzaradan as a Babylonian official at Jerusalem's destruction.

people.name: Habakkuk the prophet
people.disambiguation: The speaker identified by the biblical prophetic book.
people.summary: Habakkuk's oracles grapple with violence, injustice and divine judgment.

people.name: Zephaniah the prophet
people.disambiguation: The prophet of Zephaniah 1:1, distinct from Zephaniah the priest in Jeremiah.
people.summary: The book attributes its oracles to Zephaniah in the days of Josiah.

people.name: Haggai the prophet
people.disambiguation: The prophet of Haggai, not a later court official.
people.summary: Haggai speaks about the rebuilding of the temple in the Persian period.

people.name: Zechariah son of Berechiah
people.disambiguation: The prophet in Zechariah 1:1, not Zechariah father of John the Baptist.
people.summary: Zechariah's prophetic book begins with visions associated with the Persian-period rebuilding.

people.name: Mordecai
people.disambiguation: Mordecai in Esther, not an independently verified Persian court biography.
people.summary: Esther portrays Mordecai as Esther's guardian and a Jewish official in Susa.

people.name: Job
people.disambiguation: The central figure of wisdom literature; historical dating is not established by the book.
people.summary: The book of Job presents a man whose suffering frames dialogues on righteousness and divine justice.

people.name: Balaam son of Beor
people.disambiguation: Balaam of the Numbers oracle narratives, not an Israelite prophet of the monarchy.
people.summary: Numbers portrays Balaam as a diviner summoned by Balak.

people.name: Balak king of Moab
people.disambiguation: Balak in Numbers, not another historical king.
people.summary: Numbers presents Balak as a Moabite ruler who summons Balaam.

people.name: Elizabeth mother of John
people.disambiguation: Elizabeth in Luke, not a similarly named later person.
people.summary: Luke identifies Elizabeth as Zechariah's wife and the mother of John the Baptist.

people.name: Zechariah father of John
people.disambiguation: Father of John in Luke, not the Old Testament prophet of Zechariah.
people.summary: Luke depicts Zechariah as a priest and father of John the Baptist.

people.name: Simeon in the Temple
people.disambiguation: Simeon of Luke 2, distinct from Simeon called Peter.
people.summary: Luke describes Simeon meeting the infant Jesus in the Jerusalem temple.

people.name: Anna the prophetess
people.disambiguation: Anna of Luke 2, not Hannah the mother of Samuel.
people.summary: Luke identifies Anna as a prophetess who spoke about the infant Jesus.

people.name: Joseph of Arimathea
people.disambiguation: Joseph who buried Jesus, not Joseph of Nazareth.
people.summary: The Gospels describe Joseph of Arimathea requesting and burying Jesus' body.

people.name: Matthew the tax collector
people.disambiguation: Matthew in the Gospel lists; traditional Gospel authorship is a separate attribution.
people.summary: Matthew names a tax collector called to follow Jesus and lists an apostle Matthew.

people.name: James son of Alphaeus
people.disambiguation: Distinct from James son of Zebedee and James the brother of Jesus.
people.summary: The apostolic lists identify a James son of Alphaeus.

people.name: Simon called the Zealot
people.disambiguation: Not Simon Peter or Simon the magician.
people.summary: Luke's lists name Simon called the Zealot among the Twelve.

people.name: Matthias
people.disambiguation: Matthias in Acts 1, not Matthew.
people.summary: Acts describes Matthias being chosen to join the apostolic group after Judas.

people.name: James brother of Jesus
people.disambiguation: Do not conflate with either apostle named James without argument.
people.summary: The New Testament names James among Jesus' brothers and portrays a James in Jerusalem leadership.

people.name: Herod the Great
people.disambiguation: The Herod in Matthew's infancy narrative, distinct from his son Antipas.
people.summary: Matthew places Herod as king at the time of Jesus' birth account.

people.name: Herod Antipas
people.disambiguation: Herod Antipas, not Herod the Great or Agrippa I.
people.summary: Mark and Luke refer to Herod the tetrarch in the John the Baptist and passion narratives.

people.name: Herod Agrippa I
people.disambiguation: The ruler in Acts 12, distinct from Herod Agrippa II.
people.summary: Acts names King Herod as persecuting members of the Jerusalem church.

people.name: Paul the apostle
people.disambiguation: Saul of Tarsus, not King Saul of Israel.
people.summary: Acts and Paul's letters identify him as a missionary and letter writer in the early Christian movement.

people.name: Barnabas
people.disambiguation: Joseph nicknamed Barnabas, distinct from Joseph of Arimathea.
people.summary: Acts identifies Barnabas as a travelling ministry companion and church leader.

people.name: Silas
people.disambiguation: Silas in Acts, traditionally associated with the name Silvanus, without assuming identity from name alone.
people.summary: Acts narrates Silas' participation in Paul's journeys.

people.name: Timothy
people.disambiguation: Timothy of Lystra, not Titus.
people.summary: Acts portrays Timothy as Paul's associate; pastoral letters address a Timothy.

people.name: Titus
people.disambiguation: Titus the ministry colleague, distinct from Timothy.
people.summary: Paul's letters refer to Titus as an associate and a recipient of pastoral instruction.

people.name: Stephen
people.disambiguation: Stephen in Acts 6-7, not an apostle of the Twelve.
people.summary: Acts depicts Stephen's speech and death in Jerusalem.

people.name: Philip the evangelist
people.disambiguation: Philip among the Seven, distinct from Philip the apostle.
people.summary: Acts names Philip among the Seven and describes his ministry in Samaria and on the Gaza road.

people.name: Cornelius
people.disambiguation: Cornelius of Caesarea, not an unnamed Gospel centurion.
people.summary: Acts narrates a centurion's conversion and Peter's visit to his household.

people.name: Lydia
people.disambiguation: Lydia of Thyatira in Acts, not the territory Lydia.
people.summary: Acts introduces Lydia as a merchant who receives Paul and his companions in Philippi.

people.name: Priscilla
people.disambiguation: The woman also called Prisca in Romans, distinct from Aquila.
people.summary: Acts and Romans mention Priscilla with Aquila as colleagues in ministry.

people.name: Aquila
people.disambiguation: Aquila the tentmaker, not another person sharing a Latin name.
people.summary: Acts describes Aquila as Priscilla's husband and a colleague of Paul.

people.name: Apollos
people.disambiguation: Apollos of Acts, not Apollo the Greco-Roman deity.
people.summary: Acts describes Apollos as a teacher from Alexandria who comes to Ephesus.

people.name: John called Mark
people.disambiguation: John Mark, not John the Baptist or John son of Zebedee; traditional Gospel authorship is a separate claim.
people.summary: Acts calls this missionary companion John Mark.

people.name: Luke
people.disambiguation: Luke named in letters; the attribution of Luke-Acts is a separate historical question.
people.summary: Pauline letters refer to a Luke as a companion.

people.name: Gamaliel
people.disambiguation: Gamaliel in Acts, not every later rabbi of the same name.
people.summary: Acts names Gamaliel as a Pharisaic teacher and as Paul's teacher.

people.name: Ananias of Damascus
people.disambiguation: The disciple in Damascus, not the Ananias of Acts 5 or the high priest.
people.summary: Acts depicts Ananias receiving instructions to visit Saul after his vision.

people.name: Ananias husband of Sapphira
people.disambiguation: The Ananias of Acts 5, not Ananias of Damascus.
people.summary: Acts recounts Ananias and Sapphira withholding proceeds from a property sale.

people.name: Sapphira
people.disambiguation: Wife of Ananias in Acts 5, not another named woman.
people.summary: Acts narrates Sapphira's involvement in the episode of property-sale proceeds.

people.name: Tabitha
people.disambiguation: Also called Dorcas in Greek, not a separate person.
people.summary: Acts recounts Peter visiting the disciple Tabitha in Joppa.

people.name: Phoebe
people.disambiguation: Phoebe of Romans 16, not a figure in the Gospel stories.
people.summary: Romans commends Phoebe of the church at Cenchreae.

people.name: Onesimus
people.disambiguation: Onesimus connected with Philemon; later biographical traditions are separate.
people.summary: Paul's letter to Philemon concerns Onesimus, who is also named in Colossians.

people.name: Philemon
people.disambiguation: The addressee of Philemon, not Onesimus.
people.summary: Philemon is a named recipient of a letter associated with Paul.

people.name: Felix
people.disambiguation: Antonius Felix, distinct from his successor Festus.
people.summary: Acts reports Paul's hearing before the governor Felix.

people.name: Porcius Festus
people.disambiguation: Festus, not Felix or Herod Agrippa II.
people.summary: Acts describes Paul's hearings after Festus succeeds Felix as governor.

people.name: Herod Agrippa II
people.disambiguation: The Agrippa in Acts 25-26, distinct from his father Agrippa I.
people.summary: Acts presents Agrippa hearing Paul's defence at Caesarea.

people.name: Epaphroditus
people.disambiguation: Paul's associate in Philippians, not Epaphras in Colossians.
people.summary: Philippians describes Epaphroditus as a messenger from the Philippian church.

people.name: Epaphras
people.disambiguation: Epaphras, not Epaphroditus.
people.summary: Colossians names Epaphras as a servant concerned for its recipients.

people.name: Euodia
people.disambiguation: Euodia in Philippians, not Syntyche.
people.summary: Philippians addresses Euodia as a fellow worker urged toward agreement.

people.name: Syntyche
people.disambiguation: Syntyche in Philippians, not Euodia.
people.summary: Philippians addresses Syntyche as a fellow worker urged toward agreement.
